questions.question: What are the two main types of variables based on how they are created in Robot Framework?

options.text: Statically defined or imported variables
Dynamically created variables during execution
Compiled variables
options.explanation: Robot Framework doesn't compile variables; the types are static and dynamic

options.text: Temporary variables
options.explanation: This is not one of the two main categorizations; the types are static and dynamic

questions.question: What is the rule of thumb for priority of statically defined or imported variables?

options.text: First come, first served
Last one wins
options.explanation: 'Last one wins' applies to dynamically created variables, not static ones

options.text: Highest scope wins
options.explanation: For static variables, the time of definition matters most

options.text: Alphabetical order
options.explanation: Variable priority is not based on alphabetical order

questions.question: What is the rule of thumb for priority of dynamically created variables?

options.text: Last one wins
First come, first served
options.explanation: 'First come, first served' applies to static variables, not dynamic ones

options.text: Lowest scope wins
options.explanation: While scope matters, the rule is 'Last one wins' as long as in scope

options.text: Random selection
options.explanation: Variable resolution is deterministic, not random

questions.question: In what order do statically defined variables have priority (highest to lowest)?

options.text: Global command-line variables → *** Variables *** section → Resource files
*** Variables *** section → Global command-line variables → Resource files

options.text: Resource files → *** Variables *** section → Global command-line variables
options.explanation: Command-line variables have the highest priority, resource files the lowest

options.text: All have equal priority; last definition wins
options.explanation: There is a specific priority order based on time of definition

questions.question: Can dynamically created variables overwrite or shadow statically defined variables?

options.text: Yes, dynamically created variables have higher priority than static variables
No, static variables always have higher priority
options.explanation: Dynamic variables can overwrite or shadow static ones

options.text: Only if the static variable was from a resource file
options.explanation: Dynamic variables can overwrite any static variable

options.text: No, attempting to overwrite causes an error
options.explanation: Overwriting is allowed and expected behavior

questions.question: What happens when a local variable defined as a keyword argument has the same name as a suite variable?

options.text: Local variable shadows suite variable within keyword; suite variable returns after exit
Suite variable maintains priority regardless of local variable scope

options.text: Both variables coexist independently with different access prefixes
options.explanation: The local variable shadows the suite variable within its scope

options.text: Robot Framework raises duplicate variable name error at runtime
options.explanation: Shadowing is allowed; no error is raised

questions.question: What are the four variable scopes in Robot Framework?

options.text: Global scope
Suite scope
Test|Task scope
Local scope
Module scope
options.explanation: There is no module scope in Robot Framework

questions.question: How can global scope variables be created?

options.text: Set from command line using --variable or --variablefile (static)
Created during execution using VAR syntax with scope=GLOBAL (dynamic)
Defined in the *** Variables *** section (static)
options.explanation: *** Variables *** section creates suite scope variables, not global

options.text: Imported from resource files (static)
options.explanation: Resource files provide suite scope variables, not global

questions.question: What is the recommended naming convention for global variables?

options.text: Uppercase letters, like ${GLOBAL_VARIABLE}
Lowercase letters, like ${global_variable}
options.explanation: Global variables should use uppercase to distinguish from local variables

options.text: Mixed case, like ${GlobalVariable}
options.explanation: Global variables should use uppercase

options.text: Prefix with 'global_', like ${global_myvar}
options.explanation: The convention is uppercase letters, not a prefix

questions.question: What is the most common use case for global variables?

options.text: To define environment-specific configurations shared across all suites
To store temporary calculation results during individual test execution
options.explanation: Temporary results should use local variables, not global

options.text: To share dynamically changing data between tests within a suite
options.explanation: Suite scope variables are better for suite-specific sharing

options.text: To define test data expected to change frequently during runs
options.explanation: Global variables are for configuration consistent across execution

questions.question: How can suite scope variables be created?

options.text: Defined in the *** Variables *** section of the suite file (static)
Imported from resource or variable files (static)
Set during execution using VAR syntax with scope=SUITE (dynamic)
Defined on command line with --variable (static)
options.explanation: Command-line variables are global scope, not suite scope

questions.question: Are suite scope variables from initialization files available in lower-level suites?

options.text: No, suite scope is not recursive; use resource files to share variables across suites
Yes, they are automatically available to all child suites
options.explanation: Suite scope is not recursive; variables don't propagate to child suites

options.text: Yes, but only to immediate child suites, not deeper levels
options.explanation: Suite scope is not recursive at any level

options.text: Yes, if the child suite explicitly imports them
options.explanation: Suite variables cannot be imported; use resource files for sharing

questions.question: What happens when a suite-level variable is dynamically defined with the same name as a global command-line variable?

options.text: The suite variable shadows the global variable as long as the suite is in scope; then the global variable returns to scope
The global variable always has higher priority and cannot be shadowed
options.explanation: Dynamic suite variables can shadow global variables within their scope

options.text: Robot Framework raises an error about conflicting variable definitions
options.explanation: Shadowing is allowed; no error is raised

options.text: The suite variable permanently overwrites the global variable
options.explanation: The shadowing is temporary; global variable returns when suite exits

questions.question: What is the recommended naming convention for suite variables?
